summary: Preserve the private self-name of a named function expression for recursion without leaking that name to the outer scope.

target.notes: The inner name is visible only inside the function body; emit a private local function and assign it to the outer binding.

semantics.recursion: self reference denotes the created function object

caveats: If the inner function name is reassigned/observed via dynamic scope or function metadata, use a richer representation.

tests.name: recursive named expression
tests.input: const fact = function inner(n){ return n<=1?1:n*inner(n-1); }; console.log(fact(5));

tests.name: name does not leak
tests.input: const f = function hidden(){}; console.log(typeof hidden);
